blocks.text: Setting up your inventory system in Excel on Mac

The foundation of your inventory system is a clean, structured table. Avoid using loose cells for your product list. Instead, use Excel Tables. Select your data range and press ⌘ + T. This creates a dynamic table that automatically expands when you add new rows. It also makes your formulas much easier to read.

Use data validation to ensure your team enters consistent data. Go to Data > Data Validation > Settings. Choose List from the Allow menu. This forces users to select from a predefined list of items or statuses. This prevents typos that break your lookup formulas.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for inventory managers

items: Fn + F2: Edit the active cell content directly.
Shift + Space: Select the entire row quickly.
Ctrl + Space: Select the entire column for quick formatting.
Cmd + D: Fill the contents of the top cell down into the selected range.
Cmd + T: Convert a range of data into an official Excel Table.

blocks.text: One common mistake is storing leading zeros in product IDs as numbers. Excel often strips these zeros. To fix this, set your cell format to Text before you type the IDs. If you have existing data, use the Text to Columns feature in the Data tab to convert them.

Another issue is using VLOOKUP for large datasets. It is slow and prone to breaking if you move columns. Switch to XLOOKUP. It is faster, more flexible, and does not care if your lookup value is to the left or right of your return column.
Using Lazur to speed up your Excel workflow

Lazur works as a voice assistant that lives in your Mac notch. It helps you find features or remember how to write complex formulas without leaving your spreadsheet. Hold ⌥ + ⌘ to ask Lazur a question about what is currently on your screen.

If you are stuck on a formula, ask Lazur to explain how it works. You can also ask it to guide you through a menu path. Lazur will draw a circle around the button you need to click. This saves time searching through the ribbon menus.

Excel supports over one million rows, but performance drops if your workbook is too complex. Keep your calculations lean. Use references to entire columns sparingly. If your file is slow, check if you have excessive conditional formatting or volatile formulas like INDIRECT or OFFSET.

If you need to analyze your stock trends, use Pivot Tables. They are the best way to summarize large amounts of data without writing complex formulas. Go to Insert > PivotTable to start. You can drag and drop your product categories and stock levels to see trends instantly.

Use conditional formatting to highlight low stock levels automatically. Select your stock quantity column. Go to Home > Conditional Formatting > Highlight Cells Rules > Less Than. Enter your threshold value. Set a red fill to alert you when items need reordering.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Excel files directly?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate Excel for you. It points at things, answers your questions, and guides you through tasks one step at a time.

faq.question: Does Excel for Mac have the same features as the Windows version?
faq.answer: Most core features are the same, but some advanced tools or keyboard shortcuts differ. Lazur can help you navigate these differences on your Mac.

faq.question: How do I fix Excel stripping leading zeros from my product codes?
faq.answer: Change the cell format to Text before entering the data. If the data is already there, use the Data > Text to Columns feature to convert the numeric values back to text.
